text:
alex: FYI we just got a customer report where a canceled streaming request still shows up as full token usage in the console. can someone look?

maria: ugh. is that the chunked upload case where client aborts mid-stream?

alex: yes. they called a tool during the stream, then canceled. console shows tokens charged = full generated length + toolcall tokens. looks like retries + truncation edge.

sam: do we have correlation_id across the retry/fallback path? my hunch: fallback routing replays without the original idempotency token so both attempts are billed.

ellie: i checked logs for that customer request id. we have two entries: one routed -> region-a (timed out), then fallback -> region-b succeeded. both have different request_ids. telemetry only attributes tokens to final model instance, but billing pipeline sums raw tokens from both.

ryan: problem is partly how streaming truncation interacts with toolcalls. if the toolcall was invoked in the first attempt and then second attempt also invokes it, we double-charge the toolcall TTL. we need a de-dupe window at billing layer or an idempotency header that survives retries.

maria: proposal: require clients to send `X-Idempotency-Key` for any request that may cause billing side-effects (toolcall, tool injection). if absent, fallback to session-based id. 

sam: that helps for retries initiated by the platform, but what about mid-stream cancellations? client cancels after N tokens, we truncate and write prefix credits. current prefix crediting code writes a partial prefix then on rollback we don't decrement the buffered accounting.

alex: exact logs: `2026-03-15T18:02:11Z request=1898765432 stage=streaming-sent tokens=1200 toolcalls=1` then `2026-03-15T18:02:12Z request=1898765432 stage=abort client_cancelled=true` then `2026-03-15T18:02:13Z request=1898765432 stage=fallback-retry tokens=900 toolcalls=1 success=true` — billing sees 1200+900+toolcall*2.

ellie: I can instrument a correlation_id shim to be attached to fallback-retry logs so billing can collapse entries with same correlation within a window. but we need to be careful about legitimate retries that are distinct (e.g., client retried on purpose).

ryan: UX question for rollouts/console: should we show 'attributed tokens' vs 'raw tokens' on per-route dashboards? product asked for a single number but ops wants the breakdown to debug these cases.

maria: we should surface both. "raw tokens" = sum of all recorded tokens; "net tokens" = deduped view by correlation_id with configurable dedupe-window (default 30s). show a tooltip explaining truncation/toolcall cornercases.

sam: technical constraints: billing pipeline is batched by minute and assumes immutable events. dedupe by correlation_id requires either: 1) add correlation_id to existing billing events (cheap) and post-process dedupe in billing service, or 2) change runtime to avoid emitting duplicate events (harder). I prefer 1 for speed.

alex: are there privacy or compliance concerns with adding correlation_id? it's internal only. should be fine but check with security.

ellie: deploy-bot: patch queued for `streaming-telemetry` to include `x-correlation-id` header on fallbacks. preview: https://deploys/review/stream-telemetry/1898

deploy-bot: build passed for stream-telemetry @ 1898765450 :white_check_mark:

maria: OK next: toolcall TTL counting. current behavior: if toolcall invoked then truncated, we still count TTL as consumed. we need a rule: if a toolcall started but the tool never returned and the client canceled, refund toolcall token? or mark as partially consumed?

sam: we can't refund after the fact easily. better: change toolcall contract: toolcall tokens are charged on tool start, but we must emit an event with `toolcall_outcome` (started|completed|aborted). billing can apply a policy: refund aborted before 1s to zero, partial after 1s. we should add `toolcall_start_ts` and `toolcall_end_ts` to telemetry.

ryan: sounds reasonable. need to add to schema and update console toolcall histogram to show aborted vs completed.

alex: also thinking about routing: fallback vs model-variant replacements cause model mismatch in console attribution. we should surface a per-request routing trace in the "Route Explorer" pane so support can see which model handled which token span. minimal view: a timeline with token ranges attributed to route X or Y.

maria: that will help a lot. we can start with a sampled trace for high-value customers.

ellie: implementation plan: 1) add x-correlation-id propagation on retries/fallbacks (runtime change) 2) tag telemetry events with correlation and toolcall_outcome (telemetry schema) 3) billing: add post-process dedupe by correlation id with 30s window; show raw/net in console (product + ops) 4) small rollout via canary flag visible in console with "dedupe-mode=on" indicator.

sam: who owns the billing change? @ryan? we need a sprint.

ryan: I'll take billing post-process change. timeline: spike this sprint, PR next. need input from finance on refund rules.

alex: I'll own the runtime + headers change. ellie you own telemetry schema and console changes?

ellie: yep. will open RFC and include sample logs + migration notes.

maria: can we add a quick alert rule in dashboards to spike if raw/net divergence > 15% for any customer? that would catch regressions early.

ryan: good idea. I'll add an alert to per-customer billing dashboard (ops-only).

alex: great. thanks all. filing follow-ups: RFC in #eng-platform-docs, + a customer note template for affected customers.

maria: +1. thanks.

ellie: follow-up: I pasted a small code snippet for header usage in RFC: 
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
  X-Idempotency-Key: 6f1e2b3a-...
  X-Correlation-Id: session-abc-123
```

sam: perfect.

alex: closing thread, will update when PRs are live. :thumbsup:
